# AttuneUI: install and set up

> AttuneUI (the `@attuneui/*` npm packages) is an adaptive UI library for React. An app is a canvas of panels that rearranges itself around what the user is doing. A model (Jev, from TypeSafe) judges what the user is working on and which panels help; the library's code makes every layout decision. This file is the complete setup guide for an AI coding assistant.

## Rules to follow

- Never call the model from the browser. The model key lives only on a server. The browser store sends its request to your own server route (for example `POST /api/adapt`), and that server asks the model.
- The library decides the layout. Do not position, size, show, or hide panels yourself; render each panel's content and let `AdaptiveCanvas` place the cards.
- Every catalog needs the goal id `"unclear"` and the action id `"none"` (with `panel: null`). No panel may have the id `"unclear"`.
- Report what the user does with `store.track()` using the core signal types. The canvas reports focus, the pointer, and pointer rests by itself; the store's actions (`pin`, `dismiss`, `open`, `runCommand`, and others) log their own events.
- The app works without a model key: the server answers with a calm fallback (`neutralJudgments`), and the status reads "offline".
- Add the one required CSS rule (step 7), or leaving cards jump a cell before they fly to the dock.
- The packages are ESM only, need Node 20.19 or newer for the server, React 19, and motion 13.

## The packages

| Package | Where it runs | What it gives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@attuneui/core` | Browser and server | `defineCatalog`, `createAdaptiveWorkspace`, `createPolicy`, `createAdaptiveStore`, the snapshot, the layout policy, the grid, and `neutralJudgments`. No DOM, no React. |
| `@attuneui/react` | Browser | `AdaptiveCanvas`, `PanelCard`, `Dock`, `ChangeLine`, `useStoreCanvas`, `useAdaptive`. Peers: `react`, `motion`. |
| `@attuneui/jev` | Server only | `buildRound`, `readRound`, `askJev`, `createRealtimeJevClient`. Peer: `@typesafe-ai/sdk` 0.6.0. |
| `@attuneui/server` | Server only | `checkRequest`, `createRateLimiter`, `parseAdaptRequest`. |

## Step 1: install

In the browser app:

```sh
npm install @attuneui/core @attuneui/react motion react react-dom
```

On the server (any framework; the example uses Hono):

```sh
npm install @attuneui/core @attuneui/jev @attuneui/server @typesafe-ai/sdk@0.6.0 hono
```

## Step 2: the catalog

The catalog is the app's vocabulary: panels, goals, next steps, and how strongly each goal implies each panel (0 to 1). The model reads the titles and descriptions, so write them literally. `defineCatalog` checks it when the app starts and throws one `CatalogError` that lists every problem. Share this file between the browser and the server.

```ts
// src/catalog.ts
import { defineCatalog } from "@attuneui/core";

export const PANEL_IDS = ["tickets", "customers", "articles", "macros"] as const;
export type PanelId = (typeof PANEL_IDS)[number];
export const GOAL_IDS = ["answer_tickets", "research_issue", "unclear"] as const;
export type GoalId = (typeof GOAL_IDS)[number];
export const ACTION_IDS = ["reply_ticket", "send_article", "none"] as const;
export type ActionId = (typeof ACTION_IDS)[number];
export type RecordKind = "ticket" | "customer" | "article" | "macro";

export const CATALOG = defineCatalog<PanelId, GoalId, ActionId>({
  panelIds: PANEL_IDS,
  panels: {
    tickets: { id: "tickets", title: "Tickets", description: "Support tickets from customers, with status and priority.", icon: "Inbox", defaultVisible: true },
    customers: { id: "customers", title: "Customers", description: "The companies that use the product.", icon: "Building2", defaultVisible: true },
    articles: { id: "articles", title: "Articles", description: "Help articles that explain how to use the product.", icon: "BookOpen", defaultVisible: true },
    macros: { id: "macros", title: "Macros", description: "Saved replies the agent can reuse in a ticket.", icon: "MessageSquareText", defaultVisible: false },
  },
  goalIds: GOAL_IDS,
  goals: {
    answer_tickets: { label: "Answering tickets", description: "Reading open tickets and replying to customers." },
    research_issue: { label: "Researching an issue", description: "Looking for how something works, to answer a ticket." },
    unclear: { label: "Not sure yet", description: "Too little or too mixed activity to tell." },
  },
  actionIds: ACTION_IDS,
  actions: {
    reply_ticket: { id: "reply_ticket", label: "Reply to the ticket", description: "Write a reply to the open ticket.", panel: "tickets" },
    send_article: { id: "send_article", label: "Send a help article", description: "Send a help article to the customer.", panel: "articles" },
    none: { id: "none", label: "", description: "There is no clear next step right now.", panel: null },
  },
  goalPanelAffinity: {
    answer_tickets: { tickets: 1, macros: 0.6, articles: 0.5 },
    research_issue: { articles: 1, tickets: 0.5 },
    unclear: {},
  },
});
```

Panel fields: `id`, `title`, `description` (sent to the model), `icon` (a name your UI maps to an icon), `defaultVisible` (shown before any activity), and optional `commandExamples` (set on every panel or on none). Goal fields: `label`, `description`, and optional `notFor` (set on every goal or on none). Every goal needs an affinity entry; use `{}` for none.

## Step 3: the policy and the store (browser)

`createAdaptiveWorkspace` supplies the standard policy and infers IDs from the catalog. No policy factory or `AdaptiveSpec` is required for a basic app. Use `createAdaptiveStore` and `createPolicy` directly when extending the engine.

```ts
// src/engine.ts
import { createAdaptiveWorkspace, type AdaptiveRequest, type AdaptiveResponse, type JudgmentsWithCommand, type AnchorRef, type RelatedRecord } from "@attuneui/core";
import { CATALOG, type ActionId, type GoalId, type PanelId, type RecordKind } from "./catalog";

export type Judgments = JudgmentsWithCommand<PanelId, GoalId, ActionId>;

function linkedRecords(anchor: AnchorRef<PanelId, RecordKind>): Partial<Record<PanelId, RelatedRecord<RecordKind>[]>> {
  if (!anchor.client || anchor.panel === "customers") return {};
  return { customers: [{ itemKind: "customer", itemId: anchor.client, label: anchor.client }] };
}

async function postAdapt(request: AdaptiveRequest, { signal }: { signal: AbortSignal }): Promise<AdaptiveResponse<Judgments>> {
  const res = await fetch("/api/adapt", { method: "POST", headers: { "content-type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify(request), signal });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`The server answered ${res.status}`);
  return res.json();
}

export const store = createAdaptiveWorkspace({
  catalog: CATALOG,
  send: postAdapt,
  words: { itemWords: { ticket: "ticket", customer: "customer", article: "help article", macro: "saved reply" } },
  linked: linkedRecords,
  anchorLabel: (ref) => ref.itemKind === "ticket" ? ref.itemId : ref.client,
});
export type DeskStore = typeof store;
```

`send` must forward `signal` to fetch. The library cancels requests replaced by newer work.
`settings.layoutBehavior: "suggestions"` keeps panel placement while suggestions update; `"adaptive"` allows automatic layout. Commands and manual panel controls work in both. `settings.density` accepts `"guided"`, `"standard"`, `"dense"`, or `"auto"`. The starter defaults to `"standard"`. Persist settings with the `persist` hook and restore through `settings` if needed.

The canvas can occupy one region of an existing page. It does not require replacing the application's navigation.

## Step 4: report what the user does

Use the core signal types in `store.track({ type, panel, detail })`:

| Type | When | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item_open` | The user opened one record | `itemKind`, `itemId`, `client`, `label`, `via: "pointer"` |
| `search` | The user searched in a panel | `query` (debounce it, for example 600 ms) |
| `filter` | The user changed a filter | `label`, or `filter` as an object |
| `action` | The user did something with a record | `actionId` (an action id from the catalog), `itemId`, `client` |

```tsx
// Inside the Tickets panel
<button
  type="button"
  onClick={() =>
    store.track({ type: "item_open", panel: "tickets", detail: { itemKind: "ticket", itemId: ticket.id, client: ticket.customer, label: `${ticket.id} "${ticket.subject}"`, via: "pointer" } })
  }
>
  {ticket.subject}
</button>
```

Do not track focus, pointer moves, pins, docking, commands, or suggestions yourself: the canvas and the store's actions log them.

## Step 5: the canvas

`useStoreCanvas(store)` wires the canvas to the store. You render each card's content; the canvas places the cards in their cells and plays the staged relayout.

```tsx
// src/App.tsx
import { AdaptiveCanvas, ChangeLine, Dock, useAdaptive, useStoreCanvas } from "@attuneui/react";
import { CATALOG } from "./catalog";
import { store } from "./engine";

export function App() {
  const canvas = useStoreCanvas(store);
  const canUndo = useAdaptive(store, (s) => s.previousPlan !== null);
  const status = useAdaptive(store, (s) => s.status);
  return (
    <div>
      <header>
        <span>{status === "offline" ? "Offline: calm fallback" : status}</span>
        <ChangeLine decisions={canvas.plan.decisions} {...(canUndo ? { onUndo: () => store.undo() } : {})} />
      </header>
      <AdaptiveCanvas
        {...canvas}
        className="canvas"
        cardClassName={(p) => `card size-${p.size}`}
        renderCard={(p) => (
          <>
            <h2>{CATALOG.panels[p.id].title}</h2>
            {p.relation ? <span title={p.relation.reason}>{p.relation.tag}</span> : null}
            <button type="button" onClick={() => store.dismiss(p.id)}>Dock</button>
            {/* Your panel component goes here. Show a short summary when p.size is "compact". */}
          </>
        )}
        empty={<p>Everything is in the dock.</p>}
      />
      <Dock docked={canvas.plan.docked} label={(id) => CATALOG.panels[id].title} onOpen={(id) => store.open(id)} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

Other store actions for the UI: `pin(id)`, `unpin(id)`, `maximize(id)`, `restore(id)`, `dismiss(id)`, `open(id)`, `runCommand(text)` (a command bar), `acceptSuggestion(s)` and `dismissSuggestion(s)` (for `plan.suggestions`), `undo()`, `setSettings({ adaptive, frozen })`, and `reset()`. Read state with `useAdaptive(store, selector)`: `plan`, `status`, `goal`, `command`, `pinned`, `bigger`, `anchor`, `history`.

## Step 6: the server

The server checks the request, asks the core questions in one round with a time budget, and always answers.

```ts
// server/app.ts
import { neutralJudgments } from "@attuneui/core";
import { askJev, buildRound, createRealtimeJevClient, readRound } from "@attuneui/jev";
import { checkRequest, createRateLimiter, parseAdaptRequest } from "@attuneui/server";
import { Hono } from "hono";
import { CATALOG } from "../src/catalog";

const apiKey = process.env.JEV_API_KEY;
const client = apiKey ? createRealtimeJevClient({ apiKey, model: "jev-latest" }) : null;
const allow = createRateLimiter();

export const app = new Hono();

app.get("/api/health", (c) => c.json({ ok: true, jev: client !== null }));

app.post("/api/adapt", async (c) => {
  const refused = checkRequest({ host: c.req.header("host"), origin: c.req.header("origin"), contentType: c.req.header("content-type") }, { requireJson: true });
  if (refused) return c.json({ error: refused.error }, refused.status);
  if (!allow()) return c.json({ error: "Too many requests." }, 429);
  let body: unknown;
  try {
    body = await c.req.json();
  } catch {
    return c.json({ error: "The body is not valid JSON." }, 400);
  }
  const parsed = parseAdaptRequest(body);
  if (!parsed.ok) return c.json({ error: parsed.error }, 400);
  const { version, snapshot, command } = parsed.request;
  const { state, questions } = buildRound(CATALOG, { app: "A help desk for a small software company.", snapshot, command: command ?? null });
  const round = await askJev({
    client,
    state,
    questions,
    read: (answers) => readRound(answers, questions, CATALOG),
    fallback: { name: "fallback", answer: () => neutralJudgments(CATALOG, command ? { command } : {}) },
    budgetMs: 4_500,
    signal: c.req.raw.signal,
    logTag: `[adapt] v${version}`,
  });
  return c.json({ version, ...round });
});
```

Start it on localhost (for example with `@hono/node-server`) and proxy `/api` to it from the browser app's dev server (in Vite: `server.proxy = { "/api": "http://localhost:8791" }`). `checkRequest` accepts only loopback hosts and origins, so the dev server and the API must both run on localhost. Behind a CDN, pass `{ requireJson, edge: { secret, origin } }` and have the CDN add the secret in the `x-origin-verify` header. Keep `JEV_API_KEY` in an environment variable or a `.env` file that git ignores.

## Step 7: the CSS

The canvas draws only its layout. Style it with class names and these attributes: `data-canvas` on the grid; `data-panel`, `data-size` (`hero`, `large`, `standard`, `compact`), `data-anchor`, `data-linked`, `data-change`, `data-quiet`, and `data-front-ring` on each card; `data-ghost` on a docked card's empty slot; `data-dock-id` on each dock item. One rule is required:

```css
[data-canvas] > [data-motion-pop-id] {
  grid-area: auto !important;
}
.card { border: 1px solid #ddd; border-radius: 12px; padding: 10px 12px; overflow: hidden; display: flex; flex-direction: column; min-height: 0; }
.card[data-anchor] { border-color: royalblue; }
.card[data-linked] { border-color: teal; }
[data-ghost] { border: 1px dashed #ddd; border-radius: 12px; }
```

## Check the setup

1. Start the server and the browser app. The status reads "offline" without a key, which is expected.
2. Open a record in a panel. About a second later the canvas re-plans: the panel you worked in holds still, linked panels get their tag, and the change line says what changed.
3. With `JEV_API_KEY` set, the status reads "idle" after a round, and the goal (`useAdaptive(store, (s) => s.goal)`) follows the work.

## Going further

- An app's own features (its own event types, extra state, commands that set filters, custom suggestions) join the loop through hooks in the store config and an `extend(kernel)` function that returns extra state, actions, and hooks. Do not write a second loop.
- To keep the state in zustand, use `createAdaptiveEngine(config, { get, set })` inside `create()(...)` instead of `createAdaptiveStore`.
- To draw each card yourself, pass `card` to `AdaptiveCanvas` with a component that renders `PanelCard` with the props it receives.
- A complete example app built only from the packages: `apps/playground` in the repository (a help desk with four panels, its own data, and its own Jev server).
